title: Edgecase quality breakdown: AWQ vs GPTQ vs int8/int4
content:
PURPOSE
This is a focused, informal audit of per-slice quality deltas we observed when onboarding Llama-variant family checkpoints under several quantization pipelines: AWQ (mixed-blocks), GPTQ (residual-correction), 8-bit symmetric (int8), and 4-bit grouped (int4). Goal: identify where small global BLEU/EM/ROUGE changes hide large regressions on narrow slices (edge cases), surface candidate mitigations, and propose gating thresholds for Dedicated/Hosted rollouts.

SUMMARY FINDINGS (quick bullets)
- Global averaged metrics are small: mean delta (AWQ/GPTQ/int8/int4) vs fp16 typically within ±0.7% for generation-quality on our dev prompts.
- Several narrow slices show outsized regressions (3–12% absolute) for AWQ-int4 and GPTQ-int4 on reasoning and numeric normalization prompts.
- AWQ tends to preserve factual recall better on short-answer QA but drops more on long multi-hop prompts versus GPTQ.
- int8 is the safest overall; int4 has the best latency/cost tradeoff but requires slice-level gating or prompt-aware fallback.
- Failure modes cluster by: (a) numeric formatting, (b) instruction-following with multi-step constraints, (c) low-frequency named entities.

EXPERIMENTAL SETUP
- Model family: Llama-2-13B-refined (internal fork). Baseline: fp16. Quantized artifacts: AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4, symmetric-int8, grouped-int4 (block-size=64).
- Inference harness: local bench v0.17 (same code path as onboarding harness); batching=1 (latency SLO), max_new_tokens=256, temperature=0.0 for deterministic metrics, 3 repeats for sampling-sensitive slices (mean reported).
- Eval sets: merged prompt pool (approx 6.2k prompts) composed of: instruction-tuning subset (2k), short-answer QA (1.5k), multi-hop reasoning (800), math/numeric normalization (600), code-completion minimal (300), entity-disambiguation (500), hallucination stress tests (500).
- Slicing logic: lightweight regex + tag-based classification (see slice definitions below). Many slices overlap; we report per-slice population and also an "exclusive" slice delta where possible.

SLICE DEFINITIONS AND POPULATIONS
- reasoning-multi-hop (800) : prompts that require 2+ reasoning steps and intermediate deduction.
- numeric-normalization (600) : user-provided numbers in varied formats, require canonicalization (e.g., \"1,234\" -> \"1234\").
- short-qa-factual (1500) : short factual answers (< 30 tokens) from knowledge base.
- lowfreq-entities (420) : prompts referencing entities with <100 mentions in training dump.
- instruction-boundary (1200) : instructions with strict format constraints (lists, bullet outputs, format tokens).
- code-mini (300) : short code completion and formatting.

KEY METRICS REPORTED
- Exact Match (EM) for short-qa/numeric; ROUGE-L for longer generations; BLEU for structured answers; Accuracy for multi-choice; and a custom P-Score for instruction-format adherence (0–1).
- We report: baseline_fp16, quantized_artifact, delta_abs, delta_rel_pct (relative to baseline).

RESULT HIGHLIGHTS (abridged table)
Slice | baseline_fp16 | AWQ-int4 | GPTQ-int4 | int8 | delta_note
reasoning-multi-hop | ROUGE-L 56.2 | 48.9 (-7.3) | 51.5 (-4.7) | 54.8 (-1.4) | AWQ-int4 worst on chain-of-thought continuity
numeric-normalization | EM 82.4 | 70.1 (-12.3) | 68.7 (-13.7) | 80.9 (-1.5) | int4 large drop; pattern-based failures (commas/units)
short-qa-factual | EM 78.9 | 75.4 (-3.5) | 76.1 (-2.8) | 78.1 (-0.8) | AWQ retains more short facts than GPTQ on average
lowfreq-entities | EM 61.5 | 52.2 (-9.3) | 54.0 (-7.5) | 59.8 (-1.7) | entity hallucinations increase in int4
instruction-boundary | P-Score 0.88 | 0.76 (-0.12) | 0.79 (-0.09) | 0.86 (-0.02) | formatting tokens get corrupted in grouped-int4
code-mini | BLEU 44.1 | 41.8 (-2.3) | 40.2 (-3.9) | 43.6 (-0.5) | small regressions; int8 safe

NOTES ON TABLE: values are illustrative aggregated stats; full per-prompt CSV attached in linked_artifacts (see PR).

DETAILED FAILURE MODES (examples)
1) Numeric normalization: examples where \"1.200,00\" -> model outputs \"1,200\" (locale confusion) or emits extra decimals. Failures are deterministic under int4 in ~9% of tested prompts.
2) Multi-hop reasoning: AWQ-int4 sometimes drops an intermediate supporting fact leading to an incorrect final. Typical pattern: chain step truncated mid-sentence and subsequent steps lose reference to earlier entity.
3) Low-frequency entities: model invents plausible but incorrect attributes (birthyears, locations) under int4; confidence scores (logits) are compressed and top-1 token flips observed.
4) Instruction boundary: when asked to return a JSON blob, quantized variants occasionally omit closing braces or use wrong separators. These are low-probability but fail closed-format validators.

QUANTIZATION-LEVEL OBSERVATIONS
- AWQ: preserves many short factual tokens because of the mixed-block-aware scaling; suffers on long-range KV attention when block mismatches introduce drift.
- GPTQ: better at preserving multi-step numeric relationships but tends to lose low-frequency tokens more than AWQ in our builds.
- int8 symmetric: stable across slices; quantization noise is smaller and more uniform — lowest variance in deltas.
- int4 grouped: best cost/latency but highest slice volatility. Block size tuning (32 vs 64) shows a strong correlation with lowfreq-entity errors.

SAMPLE INVESTIGATIONS RUN (linked experiments)
- Run: quant-sweep-2025-10-21 (bucketed by blocksize, per-layer-scale diagnostics) -> found that layer 8..12 attention scales correlate with multi-hop failures (Pearson r=0.42).
- Run: prompt-perturbation-numeric-2025-10-28 -> adding explicit canonicalization instruction upstream reduces numeric EM delta by ~60% for int4 variants.

REMEDIATION STRATEGIES (short list)
- Prompt-level mitigations: if prompt classified into numeric-normalization or instruction-boundary, add a lightweight preamble (explicit format/canonicalization) + post-validate. Cheap and avoids model changes.
- Fallback routing: route high-risk slices to int8 or fp16 if latency SLO allows; tagging at request-time via simple regex is low-cost.
- Per-output validator: for JSON/code/numeric outputs run a post-check and trigger fallback or re-synthesis on failure.
- Tuning: experiment with block-size 32 for grouped-int4; prioritize per-layer scaling on mid-layers 8..12; try hybrid AWQ+GPTQ per-layer combos.
- Dataset augmentation: add targeted few-shot exemplars for lowfreq entities and numeric canonicalization to the onboarding prompt-set; re-eval.

PROPOSED GATING POLICY (working draft)
- If the request class is numeric-normalization OR instruction-boundary -> default quantized target = int8; allow int4/AWQ only if quality SLO (slice EM/Format adherence) > 95% on historical window.
- If reasoning-multi-hop and length > threshold (tokens>120) -> keep AWQ/GPTQ variants disabled unless canary pass shows <3% regression on last 5k requests.

NEXT STEPS / TODOs
- [ ] Run blocksize sweep for grouped-int4 with n=3 seeds (assigned: Ethan). Jira ML-4135.
- [ ] Implement request-time regex-based classifier for numeric/instruction-boundary (Priya) and run 72-hour canary on dev Dedicated cluster.
- [ ] Push per-layer scale logging to APM (Luca) so we can correlate failures in production traces.
- [ ] Draft gating rule YAML for ops team and surface to product-security for review (Maya).

OPEN QUESTIONS
- How to quantify "low-frequency entity" risk in customer-sensitive contexts vs internal eval? Should we weight entity errors by downstream harm (privacy/regulatory)?
- Is it acceptable to route a percentage of production numeric prompts to int8 to preserve UX? What SLA impact?

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep the dev CSVs but redact PII before archiving.
- Save a snapshot of the failing prompts for model-interpretability runs (see folder ML-explain/edgecases).
